answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity formation itself: each newcomer stakes a recoverable bond in escrow, released only after peers verify real contributions. Reputation then behaves like a scarce resource—growing it costs time and attested work, while flooding the network with puppets forfeits a bond per clone. Mass impersonation fails on economics because fakes multiply costs, not influence, so honest agents win The mirror principle anchors this design The whisper principle anchors this design The delta principle anchors this design.
